findings.summary: Video placement type lost: adapter deletes canonical `plcmt` field and `placement.placement` is sourced from deprecated `mediaTypes.video.placement` instead of canonical `mediaTypes.video.plcmt`
findings.failure_scenario: Publisher sets `mediaTypes.video.plcmt = 1` (instream) without the deprecated `placement` field. Library sets `placement.placement = undefined` (from deprecated field), adapter deletes `placement.plcmt` (the canonical value). Server receives no placement type, potentially serving wrong ad format or no ad.

findings.summary: `interpretResponse` has no try/catch around `serverResponse.body.length`; old colossusssp adapter caught and logged errors
findings.failure_scenario: Server returns null body, malformed response, or network error produces an unexpected response object. `serverResponse.body` is null/undefined, accessing `.length` throws an uncaught TypeError, crashing the bid response processing instead of returning an empty bid array.

findings.summary: `schain` always included in placement (minimum `{}`); old code only included it when `bid.ortb2.source.ext.schain` was present
findings.failure_scenario: A placement with no supply chain data now sends `schain: {}` in the JSON request. `{}` is invalid ORTB schain (missing required `ver`, `complete`, `nodes` fields), potentially causing server-side validation failure or bid rejection.

findings.summary: `page` field now sends full URL from `bidderRequest.refererInfo.page` instead of just `location.pathname`
findings.failure_scenario: Old code sent `page: '/home'`; new code sends `page: 'https://example.com/home'`. Server-side URL parsing, matching, or logging that expects a path-only value may break or produce incorrect results.

findings.summary: NATIVE bid validation stricter: now requires `bid.native.impressionTrackers` with non-empty array; old colossusssp accepted any truthy `bid.native`
findings.failure_scenario: Server returns a valid native bid with creative but without impression trackers (or with an empty tracker list). The old adapter would accept and forward this bid; the new adapter silently drops it in `interpretResponse`, reducing fill rate.

findings.summary: `buildRequests` replaces `request.data` with a hand-picked subset, silently dropping `coppa`, `tmax`, `bcat`, `badv`, `bapp`, `battr`, `device` that the `buildRequestsBase` library function sets
findings.failure_scenario: Library adds a new request field in a future version (e.g., a new consent or targeting parameter). The adapter's explicit field-whitelist reconstruction silently drops it, so the new feature never reaches the colossusssp server. Existing dropped fields like `coppa` and `tmax` are also lost from bid requests.
